Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- What the test does
  - MinpackTest.testMinpackJennrichSampson constructs a LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer, configures tight tolerances, and optimizes a Jennrich-Sampson least-squares problem. It expects the optimizer to converge without throwing and to return parameters very close to the theoretical solution.

- How the optimizer is supposed to be configurable
  - AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer sets a default VectorialConvergenceChecker in its constructor and provides setConvergenceChecker/getConvergenceChecker for customization. The optimize(...) method sets up the problem and then delegates to doOptimize() for the actual iterations.

- What LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer actually does
  - In LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer.doOptimize(), all iterative termination decisions are made using internal Levenberg-Marquardt specific thresholds: costRelativeTolerance, parRelativeTolerance, orthoTolerance, or hardcoded machine epsilon checks. The method never calls getConvergenceChecker(), nor does it reference the checker field at all.
  - The code even contains misleading comments:
    - “we use the vectorial convergence checker” (just before the convergence tests) but the following conditionals only use actRed, preRed, ratio, delta, xNorm and the LM-specific tolerances, not the external checker.
  - There is also an early-return path on orthogonality (maxCosine <= orthoTolerance) and several exception paths for “tolerance too small” when reductions are at machine precision, again independent of the convergence checker.

- Why this causes the failure
  - The bug report states that LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer ignores the VectorialConvergenceChecker parameter. The code confirms this: the checker is neither consulted nor influences termination in doOptimize().
  - In the Jennrich-Sampson case with tight tolerances, the algorithm does not stop based on the (default) vectorial convergence checker’s criteria (as intended by the framework). Instead, it keeps iterating according to its own internal conditions. This can lead to:
    - either premature acceptance at a point that fails the function’s checkTheoreticalMinParams (wrong final parameters), or
    - hitting the “stringent tolerances” exception paths (e.g., “cost relative tolerance is too small ... no further reduction ...”), which the test does not expect.
  - Given the test harness catches OptimizationException and asserts that no exception is expected, reaching these exception paths causes the test failure.

- The core fault
  - LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer.doOptimize ignores the convergence checker provided by AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer (default or user-specified). Termination is hard-wired to internal LM-specific thresholds and machine epsilon checks, contrary to the API contract and the comment claiming the vectorial convergence checker is used. This mismatch leads to non-compliant stopping behavior and the observed test failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
